acceptance: No module under `benchbox/core/**/dataframe_queries*` compares `ctx.platform` (or a lower-cased copy) with a string literal; they use the shared predicate.
A test shows an unknown engine name passed to the predicate raises instead of returning false.
Existing tests for TPC-DS rank handling on Polars and the read-primitives Dask and DataFusion paths pass unchanged.
description:
Gap. TPC-DS Q16 and Q95 carried branches comparing `ctx.platform` with `"datafusion"` while the adapter reports `"DataFusion"`; they were dead from v0.1.1 until removed in PR #4169, and nothing failed. The same mistake can be written again: `ctx.platform` is the adapter's display name (`Polars`, `DataFusion`, `PySpark`, `LakeSail`, `Dask`, `Pandas`, `cuDF`), and query modules compare it three different ways today: exact display name (`benchbox/core/tpcds/dataframe_queries/queries.py`, `_sql_rank_expression`, `!= "Polars"`), lower-cased with separator normalisation (`benchbox/core/read_primitives/dataframe_queries.py`, `_is_dask_context`, `_is_datafusion_context`), and class-internal checks in `unified_frame.py`.

Expected: one typed way to ask which engine a context runs on (for example an enum or predicate on the context), used by every query module, so a misspelt or wrong-case name is a type or lookup error, not a silently false comparison.

Guardrails: no query pattern may be selected by platform for speed without recorded complete-query timings. Search for an existing helper before adding one (`make duplicate-check-delta`). Behaviour of the three existing call sites must not change. If a static check is added, wire it into required CI in the same change.
